results.answer:
## The operative cap

**Master Services Agreement** (dated 14 March 2026, Norrvagn Group AB as "Supplier"), clause 9.1:

> "The aggregate liability of the Supplier under this Agreement shall not exceed USD 1,800,000."

That is the only liability cap in an executed contract in this matter.

## The documents do not agree

**Letter of Intent** (2 February 2026), paragraph 3:

> "The aggregate liability of the Supplier shall be capped at USD 2,500,000."

So there is a USD 700,000 gap between the LOI figure and the figure that landed in the signed MSA. The LOI is expressed as a statement of intent — "This letter records the terms on which the parties intend to proceed" — and predates the MSA by six weeks, so on its face the MSA figure governs; but if the drop from 2.5m to 1.8m was not a deliberate concession, it is worth checking against the negotiation record.

Two further points on that gap:

- The **Board Minutes** (10 March 2026) record the fee — "It was NOTED that the fee for the Services would be USD 40,000,000" — and authorise execution of the MSA, but say nothing about the liability cap. So the board papers do not confirm which figure was approved.
- The **Side Letter** (20 March 2026) does not amend clause 9. It varies only the termination notice period and adds a reporting obligation. Note, though, that it is governed by New York law ("shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York") while the MSA is governed by England and Wales — a split that could matter if a liability dispute arose under the Side Letter's subject matter.

A search for "liability" across all readable documents returns hits in only the MSA and the Letter of Intent.

## Caveats

- **One document could not be read**: the *Disclosure Letter (scanned)* returned no text. A disclosure letter is exactly where a carve-out or qualification to the cap might sit, so I cannot tell you the cap is unqualified across this matter — only across the four files I could read.
- The MSA as filed runs to 918 characters and contains only clauses 1, 2, 9, 10 and 14. If there are intervening clauses (including any exclusions from the cap for fraud, death or personal injury, or IP indemnities, which clause 9 as filed contains none of), they are not in the version on file.
- The automated check on the MSA flagged one critical issue relevant to reading clause 9.1: **"Agreement" is capitalised as a defined term throughout but no definition appears in this document.** Clause 9.1 caps liability "under this Agreement," so the term doing the work in the cap is itself undefined. It also flagged that "Pilot Period" is defined in the MSA but never used there — it is in fact used in the Side Letter, which may be the intended link.

results.answer:
**No indemnity in the four documents I could read.** I read each of them in full and searched for "indemn" and "hold harmless" — no hits.

What the four readable documents do contain on risk allocation:

- **Master Services Agreement**, clause 9.1: *"The aggregate liability of the Supplier under this Agreement shall not exceed USD 1,800,000."* That is a cap only — no indemnity, and nothing framed as a hold-harmless.
- **Letter of Intent**, paragraph 3: *"The aggregate liability of the Supplier shall be capped at USD 2,500,000."*
- **Side Letter** — deals only with termination notice during the Pilot Period, governing law, and a *"monthly service report"*.
- **Board Minutes** — fee and execution authority only.

**One caveat.** The matter has five documents, and one could not be read: the **Disclosure Letter (scanned)**, which returned no text at all. A disclosure letter is exactly the sort of document that carries or qualifies an indemnity, so I cannot tell you there is no indemnity in this matter — only that there is none in the four I could read. That file needs to be OCR'd or reviewed by eye.

Incidentally, while looking: the Supplier's liability cap differs between the Letter of Intent (USD 2,500,000) and the executed Master Services Agreement (USD 1,800,000). Not your question, but flagging it.
